ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with B and C on a horizontal base BC. Point A is above the base. Segment AH is drawn perpendicular to BC, meeting BC at H, with a right-angle marker at H. Point M lies on side AB, and segment MH is drawn. Reasoning: Since H is the foot of the altitude from A to BC, AH is perpendicular to BC. Because B and H both lie on BC, BH is along BC, so AH is perpendicular to BH. Therefore triangle ABH is a right triangle with right angle at H. In this right triangle, AB is the hypotenuse. M is the midpoint of AB, so by the right-triangle hypotenuse-midpoint theorem, M is equidistant from A, B, and H. Thus HM equals half of AB. Since AB = 13, HM = 13/2 = 6.5.

method.method_draft: Use the right-triangle hypotenuse-midpoint theorem. From the diagram/text, since H is the foot of the altitude from A to BC, AH is perpendicular to BC; because B and H lie on BC, triangle ABH is right-angled at H. The side AB is therefore the hypotenuse of right triangle ABH, and M is given as the midpoint of AB. In any right triangle, the midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices, so HM equals half of AB. With AB = 13, compute HM = 13/2 = 6.5.
